sentence: This project provides expertise and resources to design and interpret studies of drugs that target aging processes.
This project tests whether excess adenine in the tubular part of the kidney causes early kidney injury in type 1 diabetes.
This project studies how the retina's circuits for daylight vision connect to visual perception.
This project builds a platform that uses nanocarriers to load drugs into T cells, aiming to make them work better against brain tumors.
This project tries to find the genes and DNA variants behind different levels of the protein von Willebrand factor, using whole genome sequencing.
This project studies how brain reward cells change in structure, and why, after cocaine exposure following a long break from cocaine.
This project studies how stress affects thinking skills and Alzheimer's disease risk in groups at high risk.
This project tries to stop breast cancer from spreading by finding compounds and genes that block cancer cells from engulfing other cells.
This project builds computer workflows to analyze genomic, transcriptomic and single cell data and to detect mutational signatures in sequence data.
This project tests whether vitamin E can boost immune cells to help prevent estrogen receptor-negative breast cancer.
This project studies how birth timing and serotonin shape the development of brain circuits at the front of the brain in mice.
This project tries to find out how a histone variant normally found in testes, but abnormally active in cancers, contributes to cancer.
This project tests whether natural killer immune cells and a treatment that targets cancer mitochondria can together kill acute myeloid leukemia cells.
This project builds skin-like test materials, based on measured skin cancer properties, to help evaluate imaging methods for skin cancer.
This project uses high-throughput screening to find drug-like small molecules that act against viruses with pandemic potential.
This project studies how sodium and proton swapping proteins in bacteria came to work in groups, using evolutionary analysis, biophysical experiments and machine learning.
This project studies how a fetal blood vessel called the ductus arteriosus is regulated, to help find treatments for it staying open in preterm infants.
This project builds a gene therapy that delivers full-length, working dystrophin to treat muscle and heart problems in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project builds a cell replacement therapy using engineered microglia to treat diseases in which microglia are missing.
This project uses deep learning to measure kidney volume from image scans, then studies how it relates to genes, risk factors and health outcomes.
